applicability: Checking one scaffold-constrained existing-contact pitch-arrest response against a paired same-impulse control
Checking causal command timing, original-contact retention, finite actuation, and receipt reconciliation
claim: In the exact certified BR9.3 Godot/Jolt pair, the active controller begins on the first post-impulse observation, acts through finite paired actuators, retains both original already-bearing contacts, creates no new support contact, reconciles every command and receipt, remains within its declared rate and actuator limits, and reduces aggregate angular-momentum area and pitch excursion relative to a no-brace control receiving the same declared positive pitch impulse.

evidence.certification_claim_boundary: This campaign can certify only the exact BR9.0 digest-bound existing-contact brace-controller arithmetic, mirrored arrest, bounded load-rate redistribution, explicit residual, and stable-dwell handoff scope; BR9.1 reserve, friction, existing-contact-set, detector-state, finiteness, strict-field, monotonic-tick, and delayed-reaction refusal scope; BR9.2 controller-to-force-map-to-finite-paired-actuator-to-command-ledger-to-executor-to-append-only-receipt scope; and BR9.3 paired no-brace-control and active-brace Godot/Jolt program scope named by the source-pinned programs. BR9.4 is integrity-only containment and cannot substitute for a milestone program. The live pair retains the exact BR7 material scaffold: an explicit unpowered Generic6DOF guide releases sagittal X/Y translation and pitch while locking out-of-plane translation, roll, and yaw; all guide motors and springs remain off; four hinges remain passive; and two ordinary distal contacts are already bearing before the one declared positive pitch impulse. The active controller begins only on the first post-impulse observation, redistributes commanded contact loads inside the declared unilateral, friction, reserve, load-rate, and finite-actuator boundaries, and is compared with a no-brace control receiving the same impulse. Whole-system angular-momentum reconstruction supplies the aggregate external pitch-moment check. Commanded left/right shares are not measured per-foot loads. This establishes scaffold-constrained planar existing-contact pitch arrest only, not a new-contact catch step, per-foot measured load allocation, free-3D bracing or standing, articulated-limb generality, fall arrest, getting up, gait, walking, creature repair, accepted knowledge, or automatic creature guidance.

program.claim_scope: Fresh no-brace-control and active-brace Godot/Jolt worlds retain the exact unpowered planar scaffold, passive hinges, ordinary already-bearing distal contacts, finite paired actuators, command receipts, and one identical positive pitch impulse. The active controller begins only on the first post-impulse observation and reduces aggregate angular-momentum area and pitch excursion while both original contacts remain bearing and every declared rate, residual, actuator, handoff, and intervention boundary passes.

failure_boundaries: The unpowered guide materially locks out-of-plane translation, roll, and yaw
Commanded contact shares and aggregate reconstruction do not establish measured per-foot allocation
The fixture creates no new support contact and therefore proves no catch step
No free 3D bracing or standing, articulated-limb generality, fall arrest, getting up, gait, or walking is established
mechanism: After the first post-impulse observation, the active arm redistributes commanded support through finite paired joint torques while the no-brace arm receives the same impulse without that controller path. Whole-system momentum reconstruction checks only the aggregate external pitch moment.
scope: Only the exact material BR7-derived planar scaffold, rigid bodies, passive hinges, already-bearing contacts, impulse, timing, finite actuators, controller, thresholds, timestep, solver, engine, source, and BR9.3 program scope certified by br9_20260723T160129Z_4023e51f.
